title: Using AI to write better code more slowly
summary: Describes a multi-model AI review skill that finds many real bugs with few false positives and argues for using agents to write better code more slowly rather than to ship slop fast.

assertions.quote: the latest public models from Anthropic and OpenAI are good enough to find plenty of bugs in an unscrutinized codebase.

verdicts.note: AI reviewers do catch real defects missed by humans, though with notable false-positive rates; complement, not replacement.

assertions.quote: the more, different models you throw at a PR review, the less likely you are to get hallucinations or bogus bugs.

verdicts.note: Cross-model and independent review plausibly reduces shared blind spots and self-preference bias, but evidence is mostly practitioner anecdote rather than controlled comparison.

assertions.quote: I’m writing unit tests and fixing subtle flaws that pre-date the PR.

verdicts.note: Airbnb and Google migration case studies show large mechanical refactors sped up a lot with AI, though results need careful review and broad cleanup claims are mostly anecdotal.
Google: LLM migrations finished efforts stalled for years and 'saved hundreds of engineers worth of work', making previously infeasible tech-debt work possible.
Airbnb finished a migration estimated at 1.5 engineering-years by hand in 6 weeks, after Enzyme had lingered since RTL was adopted in 2020.
Anthropic usage data: 8.6% of Claude Code tasks are papercut fixes such as refactoring for maintainability, which people say would normally be deprioritized.

assertions.quote: It’s a great way to improve the overall health of the codebase while also teaching you about the odd corners of it.

verdicts.note: Agents do speed onboarding and PR summarization, but surveys and the Anthropic learning study show many users skip understanding; outcome depends on use.

assertions.quote: if you’re the kind of developer who uses agents to write multi-hundred-line PRs that you barely understand yourself

verdicts.note: Surveys (e.g. Sonar 2026) report many developers don't always check AI code before committing, despite saying they distrust it.

assertions.quote: Agents are not terribly good at architecture

verdicts.note: Humans still own constraints and tradeoffs, but models can now propose reasonable designs when given context; the gap is narrowing.
